item.title: Innovation intermediaries and capability-building: institutional, economic and social change in regional innovation systems
item.content:encoded:
Guendalina Anzolin, University of Cambridge

Simon Collinson, Zhejiang University

Federica Rossi, Università degli Studi di Modena e Reggio Emilia

Elvira Uyarra, University of Manchester

Regional innovation systems face significant challenges from digital transformation, decarbonization needs, and economic crises. Governments increasingly fund innovation intermediaries—organizations like research centres, incubators, and technology organizations—to coordinate stakeholders and bridge gaps in innovation cycles. These intermediaries shape regional development through knowledge transfer and institutional adaptation.

This special issue seeks contributions examining how innovation intermediaries interact with regional economic change and institutional evolution. The editors welcome conceptual, empirical, and policy-focused papers employing interdisciplinary approaches and diverse methodologies, spanning economic geography, innovation studies, and public policy. Contributions should address how intermediaries foster diversification, support sustainability transitions, facilitate skills development, and shape emerging markets within regional contexts.

Appel publié par Regional Studies. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Configurations of innovation intermediaries and their role in knowledge transfer, value chain upgrading, and regional diversification or resilience
  • Structural conditions leading to the emergence of specific types of innovation intermediaries
  • Relationship between innovation intermediaries and place-based, mission-oriented, or smart-specialisation policies
  • Role of innovation intermediaries in supporting regional sustainability goals, decarbonization, and circular economy initiatives
  • Innovation intermediaries as orchestrators of human-capital formation and labour-market transitions
  • Adaptation of innovation intermediaries' activities, governance, and revenue structures to new technological waves and changing funding landscapes
  • Impact of policy interventions on innovation intermediaries in specific or comparative regional ecosystems
  • Sectoral and value-chain variations in innovation intermediaries' activities and functions
  • Innovation intermediaries' contribution to market formation, including standards, certification schemes, and demand articulation
  • Novel typologies and metrics for capturing dynamic functions of innovation intermediaries
